Mansingh vs Lalu on 6 August, 2025

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 6 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 3503 of 2024
 Mansingh
 Versus
 Lalu And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Kushagra Jain, learned counsel for the appellan  conferencing.
Shri Mahesh Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the re  ORDER
The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act against the award dated 9.5.2023 passed in MACC No.92/2021.
The appellant challenges the quantum of compensation without there being any dispute about the injuries caused in the accident or liability of the Insurance Company.
2. Short facts of the case are that on 13.3.2018 at around 10.30 PM appellant Man Singh and Rahul were returning from Sailana to Jaora by their motorcycle.
When they reached at Sailana Kariya Road Sagaj Bawji, respondent No.1 came riding motorcycle No.MP-43-YD-3273 in rash and negligent manner and collided with the motorcycle of the appellant.
Because of which appellant as well as Rahul, both sustained grievous injuries.

2.1 The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20998 2 MA-3503-2024 Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him.

entities.text:
Motor NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20998 2 MA-3503-2024 Vehicles Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The claims Tribunal after assessment of evidence available on record awarded a total sum of Rs.10,61,270/- to the appellant.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that income of the appellant has not been considered properly.

He submits that appellant was earning Rs.700/- per day by doing the work of Labourer,
but the claims Tribunal has disbelieved the same without any reason and, thus, taken the income of the appellant on notional basis, which is incorrect.
He also submits that even on other heads meager amount is awarded.
His further argument is that claims Tribunal has considered the overall permanent disability at 40.5%.
Thus, compensation looking to the said permanent disability is very less.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company by drawing attention towards the findings recorded by the claims Tribunal in para 14 of the award submits that the permanent disability certificate for 45% permanent disability into right leg of the appellant, which the claims Tribunal has considered at 40.5% with respect to overall body, which is much higher than what should have been.

He further contends that even the permanent disability is itself doubtful because the appellant has sustained only fracture of femur bone and the certificate Ex.P/147 has not been proved by any Officer or Doctor from where it was issued.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
6.

From the calculation made by the claims Tribunal of the permanent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20998 3 MA-3503-2024 disability in para 14 it is very clear that the permanent disability at 45% into right leg has been treated to be permanent disability at 40.5% for the entire body.
The method of calculation does not appear to be proper.
In addition to it the appellant has not properly led evidence for establishing his permanent disability by proving Ex.P/147, which itself is not clear as it is not with respect to overall body.

In this view of the matter, this Court is of the considered view overall compensation looking to the income taken at Rs.6,000/- per month and higher degree of permanent disability, then what it should have been, at Rs.10,61,270/- is just and proper and no interference is warranted in the impugned award.
As such the present appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil Mansingh vs Lalu on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151991448/
